title: Transfusion-Associated Modulation of Clonal Dynamics (TAMCD) in Myelodysplastic Syndrome: A Falsifiable Hypothesis
content: Iron-related toxicity and confounding by indication are established considerations in the poorer outcomes observed among transfusion-dependent patients with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). This Perspective asks whether a third, experimentally testable factor also contributes: cumulative exposure to red blood cell (RBC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) that accumulate during storage. We call this hypothesis Transfusion-Associated Modulation of Clonal Dynamics (TAMCD). Rather than direct oncogenic transfer from non-malignant donor cells, TAMCD proposes an inflammatory relay: repeated transfusion pulses may selectively favor pre-existing mutant clones that resist inflammatory stress better than normal cells do. Three evidentiary levels are kept explicitly separate throughout: an epidemiologic association with storage duration — a composite exposure proxy, not an EV-specific measure; EV-associated functional activity, shown through fractionation and depletion-rescue experiments; and EV-specific molecular causality, which lies beyond what this framework can establish. A three-gate falsification program tests exposure plausibility (Gate 0), a mechanistic route with a prespecified functional readout (Gate 1), and EV-associated attribution against non-EV and iron-related controls (Gate 2). Conditions that would reject the prespecified, operational EV-associated model are specified in advance; that is distinct from excluding every possible transfusion-associated mechanism. TAMCD is a testable hypothesis, not a recommendation to alter transfusion practice.
